verdict: PPL grew revenue 12% to $2.5B as new rates took effect in Kentucky, Pennsylvania and Rhode Island, earned $367M, and raised its long-term growth target on the strength of data-center demand for power.

segments.name: Kentucky Regulated
segments.note: Louisville Gas & Electric and Kentucky Utilities — electricity and gas in Kentucky, where new retail rates took effect January 1, 2026.

segments.name: Pennsylvania Regulated
segments.note: PPL Electric Utilities — delivering electricity in eastern Pennsylvania; new distribution rates took effect July 1, 2026, plus more transmission revenue.

segments.name: Rhode Island Regulated
segments.note: Rhode Island Energy — electricity and gas in Rhode Island, with new base rates from September 1, 2026.

segments.name: Corporate & Other
segments.note: A small amount of revenue not assigned to the three utilities.

opex.name: Other operation & maintenance
opex.note: Running the grids and gas networks day to day — crews, repairs and customer service.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Spreading the cost of poles, wires, pipes and plants over their useful lives — rising as PPL invests.

opex.name: Taxes other than income
opex.note: Mostly property taxes on utility assets.

otherDetail: Other income of $22M, less interest expense of $234M on the debt that funds grid investment — a net $212M drag.
footerNote: Adaptation for a utility: fuel ($246M) plus energy purchases ($486M) are treated as the cost of revenue; the remaining operating lines mirror PPL's income statement. Segment revenues are external-customer revenues from the 10-Q segment note.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: New rates are flowing
takeaways.text: Pennsylvania revenue rose 17% after new distribution base rates took effect July 1, 2026. Kentucky grew 11% on rates in place since January, and Rhode Island 4% on rates from September — rate cases turning into revenue across all three states.

takeaways.title: A bigger building plan
takeaways.text: PPL lifted its 2027–2030 capital plan to $25B, targeting about 10% annual growth in its rate base — the asset value regulators let it earn on — and raised its long-term EPS growth target to 7–9% a year through 2030. Its 2027 EPS forecast is $2.06–$2.14.

takeaways.title: Data centers keep coming
takeaways.text: Pennsylvania's data-center pipeline grew for the 11th straight quarter to about 35.3 gigawatts in advanced planning. PPL's Invitium Energy venture agreed terms for roughly 2 GW of new generation to serve a QTS data center in Salem Township.

oneTimers: Special items cut GAAP EPS by $0.05, to $0.49 from ongoing EPS of $0.54 (non-GAAP): $44M after tax, mostly Rhode Island acquisition integration, a hold-harmless commitment and rate-case disallowances, plus IT and customer-system integration costs.
